newsitem.title: USA: Mich. board backs natural gas well royalty sale.
newsitem.headline: Mich. board backs natural gas well royalty sale.

text.p: The Michigan state administrative board has approved sale of the state's royalty interests in certain natural gas wells, Gov. John Engler announced Friday.

The sale to an affiliate of Bear, Stearns & Co. Inc. is expected to bring in $31 million in new revenues for environmental cleanup as part of a tax credit capturing arrangement through 2002, Engler said in a prepared statement.

The Bear Stearns affiliate paid $4.5 million upfront to the Michigan natural resources trust fund to purchase the interests and will provide quarterly payments to the state, said Maureen McNulty, spokeswoman for the state budget department.

In turn, the affiliate can take advantage of federal income tax credits established in the 1970s to encourage production of non-conventional fuels, McNulty said. Those federal credits expire at the end of 2002, she noted.
Revenue from the sale has already been appropriated for fiscal 1997 for cleanup and pollution prevention programs and included in the fiscal 1998 budget recommendations.
The proposed sale, which the board approved on Tuesday, holds the trust fund harmless, McNulty said.
Royalties from the wells flow to the trust fund and that revenue stream cannot be reduced by the sale, McNulty said.
